title: Short Bio
text:
My expertise is in Statistics, with a focus on Bayesian inference and causal reasoning.



Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (Milan)

2024–present: Adjunct Professor (Statistical Inference)

2011–2024: Full Professor of Statistics

2019–2024: Head, Department of Statistical Sciences

Previous Institutions

1990–2011: Full Professor of Statistics, Università di Pavia

1987–1990: Associate Professor of Statistics, Università L. Bocconi, Milan





Main topics: Bayesian statistics; causal inference and AI; graphical models; Bayesian experimental design; reproducible research.
Author of 50+ publications in peer-reviewed journals.
ORCID: 0000-0002-1252-5926




My teaching experience spans undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral courses in Statistics. I have also held leadership roles as coordinator of master’s-level programs and as a member of a PhD steering committee.





Fellow, International Society for Bayesian Analysis

title: Research
text:
Causal Discovery. How do we learn a causal model? Refs: Biometrics (2024) • Biometrics (2021)
Causal Artificial Intelligence. Causal reasoning is key to enhance general AI; DAGs provide a practical framework. Tutorial (PDF)
Replication Studies. Was a beneficial treatment effect truly reproduced in follow-up studies? Refs: TEST (2025) • Psychological Methods (2024)
Bayesian Experimental Design. Using priors/Bayes factors to plan studies for model discrimination and power. Refs: Statistical Science (2024) • TEST (2023)
Bayesian Mendelian Randomization under Heterogeneity. Cluster heterogeneous causal effects and handle pleiotropy with robust priors.
